items.text: The original source of this table's data (ad_groups) cannot be located anywhere in the Oracle database. The same issue affects several other related tables, including ADJ_CD_DIM, TX_TYPE_DIM, POS_ITEM_TYPE_DIM and OPERATOR_DIM.
A single confirmed process updates this table on a daily schedule, and every row carries the same source label ('HQ') with no exceptions. No other process competes to update this table.
This table has no placeholder 'unknown' row and no duplicate business keys, unlike most other similar tables. It is clean on both counts.

A generic process that creates placeholder rows is technically connected to this table, the same one used for OPERATOR_DIM. Unlike OPERATOR_DIM, where this process created a large share of the rows, here every row is a normal, fully approved record: this process has never actually run against this table.

This table was not part of a group of related tables retired in 2015-2016. Its schedule start date lines up with when it first went live, not with an older process being shut down. Caveat: the file used to check this carries its own warning that it may be incomplete, so this is not full proof the table was never affected by a similar retirement.

The placeholder-creation process file carries a leftover description referring to a different, unrelated table. This is a copy-paste artifact, not a sign that the wrong table is affected: the file's actual behavior confirms it targets AD_GRP_DIM.

items.text: Where this table's data actually originates has not been confirmed. A connected table's source was found to live behind an external system named HQAnalytics; whether this table's source lives behind the same system is plausible but unconfirmed
items.note: This is the confirmed active process updating the table, so confirming its true source system matters for planning what the migration needs to replace

items.text: It is not confirmed what would cause the placeholder-creation process to run against this table, though there is no evidence it ever has
items.note: Lower priority than for OPERATOR_DIM since it has clearly not fired here, but the same process is shared across several tables and its real triggering conditions are still unknown
